tagline: Ten miles of red sandstone that once played Mars.
intro: Valley of Fire Road comes in across open desert from Interstate 15, pays at the west entrance station and crosses the southern part of the park for about ten miles. The country beside the road turns colorful there, bright red Aztec sandstone set among gray and tan limestone mountains, old dunes turned to stone that look to be on fire when the sun strikes them.

Civilian Conservation Corps crews built campgrounds, trails and stone cabins here from 1933, and it is Nevada's oldest state park. Later the outdoor scenes of Mars in Total Recall were shot almost entirely in the valley.

moments.title: Mouse's Tank and Atlatl Rock
moments.text: Two of the easier petroglyph sites to reach, with rock art left by Ancestral Puebloan farmers from the Moapa Valley, who probably came here to hunt and gather.

moments.title: Elephant Rock
moments.text: By the east entrance a quarter-mile trail from a roadside lot leads to a sandstone arch that looks like an elephant, on a knob rising 120 feet above the road.

practical: A state park entrance fee is charged to drive the road between the west and east entrance stations. The park closes at sunset except to campers, and closes to all visitors each year from December 1 through December 14.
